topic: What antenna aperture size trade-offs exist between LEO and GEO satellites when optimizing gain and portability for CMOS-based ground terminals?
consensus_response: LEO satellites' smaller beam sizes increase interference, reducing capacity. GEO satellites' larger beams mitigate interference but introduce propagation delay. Phased array technology enhances beamforming and null-steering, mitigating interference. Optimizing antenna aperture size balances gain, portability, and beamforming to maintain link quality.
reference_context: SatCom systems involve trade-offs between LEO and GEO satellites, considering factors like beam size, interference, and propagation delay.
